propositions: Plans assert that named modules provide or lack capabilities, but those assertions are false against the actual codebase (e.g., plan claims signing in completion.py when it is actually in rebar.signing)
The existing E4 criterion misses capability-surface mismatches because module existence checks pass but specific capability presence/absence claims are unverified

A new advisory, code-grounded, agent-tier criterion must be added to the G6/E4 rubric family that verifies both directions: module provides claimed capability (dc58, db7b) and module does not provide supposedly-absent capability (5886)
The criterion must be registered in registry.CANONICAL_LLM, CODEBASE_GROUNDED, and AGENT_TIER with routing entry, rubric prompt, and guide section to pass packaged validation
Deterministic unit tests and a bounded sanity check with 3 E1-verified misses (must-fire) and 3 clean plans (must-not-fire) must validate recall >=2/3 and advisory posture (never blocks)
The criterion must auto-flow into the standing effectiveness recorder with zero per-criterion wiring, feeding the advisory-to-blocking promotion gate as a future dogfood-gated change
